$comment: Kino plugin contract, apiVersion 1 to 11. The single source of truth for every number and rule a plugin meets. The app checks each value against its own code, and a test in the app pins this file to it; sdk/validate.mjs, sdk/run.mjs and the guide's tables read this file.

catalogOnly.$comment: "catalogOnly": true (Kino 0.9.54, additive: no apiVersion, valid at every one, an older Kino ignores the field). The plugin lists and describes titles and plays none: resolve is not required, one of atLeastOneOf is, forbiddenCapabilities and forbiddenFields (streamHosts, and browser only as true: "pages" reads pages for the catalog) are refused. Kino never calls its resolve, never lists it as a source of a title (search, Ver en otros plugins, Buscar dónde verlo, the player's Servidor) and sends its titles to the person's other sources. For Kino 0.9.53 and older also declare and export resolve (throwing not_found) and search or home.
catalogOnly.notBooleanMessage: The "catalogOnly" field must be true or false
catalogOnly.forbidsMessage: A "catalogOnly" plugin can't declare "{name}": it doesn't play videos

playerMessage.es: {name} solo muestra el catálogo: no reproduce videos. Busca este título en tus otros plugins.
playerMessage.en: {name} only shows the catalog: it doesn't play videos. Look for this title in your other plugins.

catalogOnly.resolveNote: catalogOnly: Kino {fromApp} y posteriores nunca llaman resolve ni sign; solo un Kino anterior, que no conoce el campo

english.$comment: Kino 0.9.55, apiVersion 9 (below it, and on an older Kino, the keys are unknown and ignored, never checked): the English variant of a setting's label, hint and confirm, of an option's and a list field's texts, and of section.label. Same limits as the base field (confirmEn only where confirm is, and only with it). The base text is the Spanish default and the fallback; Kino shows the variant when it speaks English. Other languages: unknown keys, ignored.

loadingElement.$comment: Kino 0.9.64, additive (no apiVersion): { type: "loading", text?, textEn? } draws a spinner with the text (else Kino's «Cargando…»). Answer at once with the tab's shell plus a loading element and a refreshMs, and the next call fills it in. From Kino 0.9.64 the panel context carries features: ["loading"]; an older Kino sends no features and drops the element as an unknown type, so check context.features and answer a status line there instead.

anyHost.$comment: A host reached ONLY through an approved fetchHosts "any" (not declared, not a typed server): https on port 443, a public IPv4 literal or a dotted public name (a single-label name such as router is refused), on every redirect hop and for the hidden page's start address too. Each such request spends a budget on top of maxRequestsPerCall: perSite in perSiteWindowMs (a site is the registrable domain, so its subdomains count together) and perPlugin in perPluginWindowMs, refilled continuously and kept per plugin for the whole app (a runtime that closes and reopens keeps it). nuvioPerSite/nuvioPerPlugin: a converted Nuvio scraper's, scaled with its larger per-call cap. Over budget the request fails with errorCode, never queued. Declared hosts (insecureHttp ones included) and typed servers keep their own rules and never spend it. The hidden page (kino.browser) under the grant: its start address and every later top-level navigation of a capture (always for a CloudStream page) follow one rule: a declared or typed host by its own rules, any other host https on port 443 at a dotted public name (not limited to the plugin's hosts); on the proxy path a main-frame server redirect target may be contacted once before the capture ends blocked (detection, not prevention); subresources stay any public host (never the LAN) and spend no budget. From Kino 0.9.55.

browser.onlyWhen: the person pressed play, or a download the person started (never a background resolve such as the live zap's resolve ahead, which Kino skips for a browser plugin); a download's capture never waits for another page: busy at once

captureAll.options: captureAll (every matching request until the page settles), alsoMatch (more patterns, only with captureAll), waitForCookie (a cookie the page must also hold; alone: a cookie-only page with no match), returnCookiesOnTimeout (a timeout answers what the page had, with timedOut, instead of the timeout error)
captureAll.rules: match and alsoMatch are searched anywhere in each URL, case-insensitively unless the pattern starts with (?-i); requests are deduplicated by URL, the primary match (the first request matching match) first; with waitForCookie the page never autoplays and the settle starts once both the match and the cookie hold; captureAll with waitForCookie needs a match; the answer adds its keys only when one of these options was used

page.onlyWhen: the person is using the app: their own search, Home, list, title or play (a resolve also for a download they started); never a background call (prewarm, the live zap's resolve ahead, sync, update checks), and a list's read only with the app in front. Never clicks, taps, types or scrolls: only a check that completes with no input passes
page.topLevel: every top-level navigation and the document read stay on the plugin's kino.fetch hosts (https); else blocked, no HTML

tracking.consentLine: Le contará a {hosts} qué ves y cuándo lo terminas
tracking.consentLineNoHosts: Le contará al servidor que escribas en su configuración qué ves y cuándo lo terminas

segments.consentLine: Agrega el botón para saltar la intro y los créditos

kinoDevice.$comment: kino.device (Kino 0.9.55, every apiVersion): the UI Kino shows on this device, "tv" or "phone" (a tablet gets whatever Kino shows it, usually "phone"). Undefined on an older Kino. The Node kit says "phone" unless run.mjs gets --device tv or the environment has KINO_DEVICE=tv.

kinoSeed.$comment: kino.seed(session) (Kino 0.9.55, every apiVersion): a plugin shares ONE anonymous, free guest session of its source so people in regions that cannot log in have live sessions to seed from. Best-effort and synchronous: it answers nothing and never throws into the plugin. Kino keeps only the allowed keys (each a short string or a finite number), drops the whole thing unless the three required ones are present and non-blank, and sends it to Kino's error board only when the plugin's telemetry consent is on. Absent on an older Kino: feature-detect with typeof kino.seed === "function". The Node kit has it, sends nothing and logs which keys Kino would keep.

byTitle.$comment: Kino 0.9.55, apiVersion 9 (below it the prelude drops title and year, so the query needs ids; kino.meta.byTitle is absent): kino.meta({ type, title, year? }) instead of ids (ids win when both come). Kino searches TMDB (type's endpoint, es-MX, first page) and keeps a hit whose es-MX or original title equals the asked one once both are normalised (lowercase, no accents, punctuation as spaces); with a year, that exact year wins, else one within yearSlack. A tie (same title and year, or same title and no year) or no match answers null, never a guess. Then the answer is the ids lookup's, same shape, cache (keyed by type, normalised title and year), budget and timeout. year without title, a bad title or a bad year: invalid_request.

kinoTmdb.$keyOrder: Kino's own key first, behind its cache, in-flight dedup and the two kinoKey limits; the person's key (their Ajustes setting, else a Stremio addon's they agreed to) only when Kino's key gets one of personKeyOn; with neither, a cached copy up to staleMaxDays old, else rate_limited (unavailable when TMDB refused Kino's key). no_tmdb_key only on a build without a key of Kino's and a person without one. A key a plugin keeps in its own settings is never read.
